wa_let_it_burn.primary: Colchuck Lake outlet into the west cirque

why.Aasgard-side lakeshore, slide alder, lef: When the outlet at the lake's north end is awkward to cross, or when you want to come in from the Aasgard side by the gully; longer, with a short bushwhack through alder.

wa_liberty_bell_beckey_route.primary: Blue Lake Trail to the Liberty Bell-Concord notch

why.Early-season snow gully to the notch: Spring to late June after the highway opens, when the approach gully is still full of snow and the boot path is buried; carry an ice axe and crampons for the icy morning snow.

wa_liberty_cap_ptarmigan_ridge_finish.primary: Mowich Lake, Spray Park and the Ptarmigan crest

why.White River, St. Elmo Pass and across th: When the Mowich Lake road is closed or snowed in, and for parties without a car shuttle, since it returns to the White River car after the Emmons descent; longer and crosses more glaciers.

wa_liberty_crack.primary: East Face from the SR-20 hairpin pullout

why.Early-season snow and moat at the East F: Late spring and early summer, once the highway is open but snow still buries the talus under the wall; the snow firms up icy overnight, so bring an axe and traction.

wa_lichtenberg_mountain_west_face_west_r.primary: Smith Brook road trailhead via Union Gap

why.Crest trail north from Stevens Pass: When the Smith Brook road is still under snow or you would rather avoid the gravel road; a few miles longer, and a good choice for a one-way trip along the crest.

wa_little_annapurna_south_slopes.primary: Aasgard Pass and the Core, snow-free

why.Aasgard Pass and the Core with snow: Early summer and the shoulder seasons, when the pass still holds snow; same line, but bring an ice axe and crampons and take care descending the softened snow in the afternoon.

wa_little_big_chief_mountain_northeast_f.primary: Middle Fork Snoqualmie to Dutch Miller Gap

why.Necklace Valley and La Bohn Gap from the: When the Middle Fork road end is unusable, or when making the climb part of a through-trip across the divide; longer, and it joins the standard line at the gap.
why.Pete Lake and Summit Chief camp from the: When coming from the east side or combining with Summit Chief, to reach the northeast basin without going through the gap; a different, longer way that meets the route higher up.
why.Waptus River and Lake Ivanhoe from Salmo: When starting from the Salmon La Sac side, or on a multi-day trip through Waptus Lake; long, with a river ford that is serious at high water and steep lakeshore snow early on.

wa_little_tahoma_east_shoulder.primary: White River Campground and the Wonderland Trail to Summerland

why.Fryingpan Creek, Summerland and Meany Cr: The shorter, usual start once the Fryingpan Creek trailhead and its bridge reopen, in the early July to early August window; skips the extra walk in from White River Campground.
why.From Paradise across the Cowlitz and Ing: Late autumn through spring, while the White River road to Summerland is shut; the Paradise road stays open much later, at the cost of crossing the Cowlitz and Ingraham glaciers.

wa_lizard_mountain_south_route.primary: From the north — Cascade Pass and the glacier corridor

why.From the south — Downey Creek and Bachel: Once the Suiattle road and trails reopen, when starting from the south end of the corridor or finishing a through-trip; brushy Bachelor Creek and a cold fast ford make it harder at peak melt.

why.Cave Ridge traverse from Alpental: Late season, once the snow has melted out and the Commonwealth Basin turns to brush and loose scree and talus; it skirts that lower basin entirely.

wa_monument_peak_pasayten_scramble.primary: Lower Monument Basin and the left-angling ramp

why.From Slate Pass by Robinson Creek and th: When coming from the Harts Pass side to avoid the brushy, unmaintained Monument Creek trail and the Eureka Creek ford; an easier walk but not shorter, usually a two-day trip.

wa_mount_anderson_eel_glacier.primary: Dosewallips road walk, West Fork to Anderson Pass and the tarn camp

why.East Fork Quinault and Enchanted Valley: When the Dosewallips road washout and its long road walk or the West Fork fords at high water are unappealing, or when crossing the Olympics; longer but entirely on maintained trail.
